root_causes: The planner repeatedly selected Wait for Agent 0 and Explore[dining_room_1] for Agent 1 even after the relevant room and table had already been identified, leading to no progress on remaining propositions.
There was no effective mechanism to detect that exploration was no longer yielding new information or useful objects, so the system kept issuing redundant Explore actions.

The task decomposition did not properly map all required objects (especially the missing plate and possibly a second glass or forks for the second setting), leaving the system with incomplete actionable targets despite the task still reporting 3/10 propositions completed.

The stopping/termination criterion appears to be misaligned: the episode ended and was marked as overall success despite only 3/10 propositions reported as complete and the robots still holding objects instead of having finished the placements.

Action selection lacked a recovery or re-planning step when progress (in terms of propositions completed) plateaued, causing a long loop of low-reward actions rather than switching to targeted placement or searching in new areas.
improvement_suggestions: Introduce a progress-monitoring module that detects when completed propositions have not increased over several steps and triggers re-planning instead of continuing the same Explore/Wait loop.

Refine the task-to-object mapping to ensure all necessary objects (2 plates, 2 glasses, 2 forks per setting) are explicitly included and tracked so the planner knows exactly what remains to be found or placed.

Add an exploration saturation check: when Explore in a given room has been executed multiple times with no new objects or information discovered, the planner should mark that region as exhausted and either search other rooms or switch to placement actions.

Improve the termination condition to require that all task propositions (or an equivalent high-level goal state, such as both place settings fully laid out) are satisfied before labeling the episode as success.

Incorporate goal-directed search and placement heuristics (e.g., if the agent is holding a plate and knows the table location, prioritize PlaceOn[table] over further exploration) to reduce unnecessary wandering.

Penalize repeated no-op-like action patterns (e.g., consecutive Explore in the same small area with no new observations) more strongly in the reward function to discourage oscillation and encourage policy adaptation.

Log and utilize per-object state (found, picked, placed) in planning, so that once an object is picked up (like plate_0), the planner immediately plans a placement sequence rather than further exploration.
overall_assessment: Despite being marked as a success, the trajectory shows clear inefficiencies and likely incompleteness, with the agents stuck in a long exploration/wait loop and only partial task satisfaction. Execution quality is moderate at best due to poor progress monitoring and termination logic.
task_instruction: Help me set the table for 2 people in the dining room. Place 2 plates, 2 glasses, and 2 forks at each setting, and make sure to place them next to each other.
